To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the dose distributions of Gamma Knife calculated with PENELEOPE are affected by the presence of the bone- and air- tissue interfaces, the effect depending on the position of the isocentre.
the presence of bone and/or air inhomogeneities in the Leksell Gama Knife dose distributions can lead to underdosages in the target region.
the presence of bone and air tissue inhomogeneities can lead to important differences in the dose distributions calculated for the Gamma Knife.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of bone and air inhomogeneities in the dose distributions of Leksell Gamma knife®.
the study of the effects of bone- and/or sinuses-tissue interfaces on the dose distribution in the brain.
the study of the effects of the presence of bone- and/or sinuses on dose distributions of the Gamma Knife.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
bone- and air-inhomogeneities should not be neglected when calculating the dose distributions of Gamma Knife® treatments.
bone- and air-heterogeneities produce a non-negligent effect on the dose distribution of the Gamma Knife, but it is not so significant as the one produced by the collimation of the source channels.
the presence of the bone- and air-interfaces should be considered in the dose calculation for Gamma Knife treatments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, for the Leksell Gammaknife®, the bone- and air- inhomogeneities are not negligible for dose calculations in the proximity of the skull and the frontal or maxillar sinuses, but they do not affect the dose at the isocenter.
the presence of the skull produces a small underdosage at any point in the phantom, whereas the air-tissue interfaces produce a large underdosage nearby the separation surfaces.

the presence of the skull and the frontal or maxilla sinuses produces underdosage in the isocentre of the Gamma Knife, and that the underdosage is more pronounced when the isocentre is closer to these structures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dose distribution of the Gamma Knife is affected by the presence of the skull and the sinuses, and this effect must be taken into account for the treatment planning of the Gamma Knife.

the use of heterogeneous phantoms is mandatory in order to correctly calculate the dose distribution of the Leksall Gamma Knife®, particularly for the treatment of lesions near the bone- or air-tissue interface.
the dose calculation for heterogeneous phantomies should be performed with a detailed geometry of the Gamma Knife and with a realistic model for the source configuration.
